text.en:
A Victorian viscount belonging to a branch of House Caster. His house holds territory in the northern parts of Victoria and is known for their martial prowess. A veteran soldier, having led troops against the remnants of Gaul and answered the Duke of Caster's call to war, he is also an experienced field medic.
Harold joined Rhodes Island of his own volition following the disclosure of the above information. At his own request, he currently serves as a medic in various operations.
text.zh:
维多利亚的子爵，属开斯特家族旁支。领地位于维多利亚中北部，在开斯特一系中颇负武名。本人常年率领领地中的征召军对抗高卢残党，且时常响应开斯特公爵的号召出征，拥有极为丰富的战争经验，以及在这个过程中磨练而来的临床医疗经验。
——在公示了以上身份信息后，哈洛德以个人身份志愿加入罗德岛。并且，出于本人的坚持，现作为医疗干员活跃于各类任务中。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Harold shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12u/L
Operator Harold rarely comes into contact with Originium.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员哈洛德没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.12u/L
干员哈洛德甚少接触源石。

text.en: Regardless of what impression Harold's background left on Rhodes Island leadership, his arrival certainly left an impression on many operators. The sight of a well-dressed Victorian noble who had just elegantly introduced himself in impeccable King's Victorian bringing out a burdenbeast foal and introducing it with a completely different level of passion is bound to leave an indelible mark on the memory. The first thing he did after that was request a burdenbeast pen. While there was some befuddlement over him claiming to be a veterinarian, it soon became clear that he was serious about being a vet here, given how much time he spends in the pen and the number of veterinary and ecology-related papers he has published in Rhodes Island's internal newsgroup. Today, his name is widely known amongst Rhodes Island's pet owners, who have seen their beloved pets become happier and healthier under Harold's care, and learned more about animals under his tutelage. Not everything has been smooth sailing for him at Rhodes Island, however. It was a sunny afternoon, and Harold was explaining burdenbeast facts to operators visiting the pen. He asked for a volunteer to demonstrate milking, and he got one: Siege, who happened to be at Rhodes Island that day. For the first time since he arrived, Harold looked uncomfortable. Though he quickly recovered and began instructing her on milking, it was obvious to everyone that his movements were stiffer than usual. Very well, I admit it, I was startled at first. But then I realized I was just an old man who came here to get his men's illnesses treated and enjoy some peace and quiet. What Her Royal Highness gets up to and where is none of my business, is it? Oh, Her Royal Hi—I mean, Siege said she was interested in the habits of burdenbeasts. I should get the materials together now. Ta-ta!
text.zh:
不论哈洛德的背景给罗德岛上层带来的印象，他本人的到来，对许多罗德岛干员来说也是颇具冲击性的。
毕竟，一个衣冠楚楚的维多利亚贵族在用一串标准到不能再标准的维多利亚语进行自我介绍后，再牵出一头幼年驮兽并一改刚才的优雅，以一种热情的态度进行介绍时，那种强烈的反差，任谁都难以忘记。
在那之后，他立即申请了一间中型的养殖间，用于养殖驮兽，虽然一开始大部分人对于他自称是兽医感到有些茫然，但是看到他每日频繁地进出养殖间，并且一篇又一篇与动物医疗以及生态相关的论文在罗德岛内部的论坛上发表，越来越多的人开始意识到，哈洛德似乎是真的想要在这里发展兽医业务。
如今，哈洛德已经成了饲养宠物的干员们之中的名人，他们的宠物不仅在哈洛德的照料下焕发了比以往更旺盛的活力，而且，在哈洛德的教导下，这些干员本身对于动物的理解也在不断提升。
不过，他在罗德岛的生活也并不总是顺风顺水。
那是个阳光明媚的午后，哈洛德像往常一样，在养殖间中对着那些来见习或者凑热闹的干员滔滔不绝地讲述着有关驮兽的知识。
在讲到挤奶的时候，他询问干员们之中是否有志愿者，而走出人群的那一个，是恰好在那天返回罗德岛的推进之王。
接下来的场面显得有些滑稽，哈洛德第一次在干员们面前表现得有些狼狈。虽然他很快反应了过来并开始指导推进之王挤奶，但在场的所有人都看得出来，他的动作和平时相比有些僵硬。

好吧，我承认，一开始我确实有点愣住了。不过，转念一想，我只是个来给部下治病顺便疗养的小老头，高贵的殿下出现在哪里和我又有什么关系？哦，推进之王殿——呃，推进之王小姐还说对驮兽的习性挺感兴趣的，我要去准备准备我的课件了，再会！

text.en:
[Operation Log]
May 23
Doctor told me that Harold's family asked us to keep a close eye on his sleep and diet, and especially to limit his alcohol intake. I was therefore asked to have a look at his room at night.
I had said hi to him earlier in the evening, when I saw him heading into his room from the corridor, so I thought he'd gone to bed when I saw a bump under the blanket, only to realize that it was a pillow and that he had snuck out.
I frantically searched everywhere, only to find him in the cafeteria, where he was drinking with the soldiers he brought with him to Rhodes Island. I was fuming, of course, but he didn't seem the slightest bit agitated when he saw me, instead calling me over.
They explained that one of the soldiers had been having nightmares of the war. Harold told me that he put the pillow there so I wouldn't worry. They'd gotten up in the middle of the night to comfort their comrade by having a drink with him.
I sat down with them and listened to their war stories, and how their comrade came down with his condition. It was moving.
Harold said they didn't drink because they wanted to; they drank to drown their sorrows. I can't help but feel sorry for them. Maybe I can talk to the Doctor, see if we can relax things a little...

Come to the control room and check out the security footage, when you can. They were very much enjoying themselves until they noticed you, at which point they exchanged a look and put on that pity play. Then they started partying again as soon as you left.
Can't have been the first time they put on that act either, given how smooth the whole thing was. No wonder the Doctor gave me a heads-up.
- Closure

[Operation Log]
May 24
Thanks for the heads-up, Closure! I won't be fooled again.
Nothing happened today.

You might've fooled me too, if there weren't a few more hidden cameras Harold didn't know about.
You got so touched by their stories that you ended up drinking with them all night!
We need a different person on this job, Doctor. The kids don't stand a chance against these old slicksters.
- Closure
text.zh:
【执勤记录】
5月23日
博士告诉我，哈洛德先生的家人请我们多多关注他的饮食和作息，尤其是不能让他过量饮酒，特地请我们在夜晚检查他的宿舍，我就去看了一眼。
傍晚的时候我还在走廊和他打了个招呼，看他是往自己的宿舍去，所以我以为他已经睡下了。看到被子鼓起来时，我原本要走了，结果仔细看看，发现那竟然只是一个枕头，他不知道在什么时候溜出去了！
我赶紧去找他，找到一半，听到食堂那边有动静，过去一看，发现他正在和他带上罗德岛治病的士兵兄弟喝酒，我本来有点生气，但他见到我之后也没有很慌张，反而向我招手，让我过去。
我凑过去才发现气氛不是很对，听他们解释，原来其中一位士兵兄弟精神上有些紧张，做了和战场有关的噩梦。哈洛德告诉我说，枕头的事只是因为不想让我操心，他们几个半夜起来就是为了安慰这个兄弟。而他们兄弟之间互相安慰的方式，就是喝点小酒。
他们拉着我坐下，给我讲了一些他们战场上的往事，也讲了这位士兵兄弟为什么会得病，听得我也挺感动的。
而且，听到哈洛德说，他们喝酒有的时候也不是自己想喝，只是需要找点东西麻痹自己，我也挺难受的，我打算和博士聊一聊，我们或许可以对他宽容一点……

来主控室，我可以给你看看当时的监控录像。他们一开始喝得可开心了，注意到你靠近以后，互相递了个眼神就开始摆出那副愁云惨淡的架势。把你骗走之后，他们又大喝特喝了起来。
一整套操作的流畅程度和演技之高超证明他们拿这套东西骗过不止一个人。难怪博士还给我提了个醒。
——可露希尔

【执勤记录】
5月24日
多亏了可露希尔小姐的提醒，今天要是再发生这种事，我一定不会上当的！
今日无事发生。

啧，如果不是哈洛德对罗德岛还不够了解，有几个隐蔽的机位他还没摸清楚，说不定还真被你们混过去了。
你小子根本就是被他们拉着听故事听感动了，然后陪他们喝了一宿！
博士，换人执勤吧，年轻人根本玩不过这群老油条的。
——可露希尔

text.en: 'General, I heard you plan to assault the pass from the front. May I offer my opinion?' 'You're that medic they were talking about? Are you questioning my strategy?' 'No, of course not, just making a few observations. See, this is the lay of the land, with one pass through the middle, and three tiny trails providing access from the side. 'If I were the enemy, and I was facing a commander known for her frontal assaults, I would strengthen my defense down the middle, while sending people down the trails to flank the enemy.' 'Makes sense. Are you suggesting I split the squad and send people to attack down the trails?' 'No, no, only third-rate tacticians think that variety is the ultimate goal of tactics. But only the most cunning can fool everyone, because you can't help but leave traces of their own work.' 'I don't get it.' 'It's simple. Would you be willing to split your squad if I suggested it?' 'No, that would be boring.' 'Exactly. I just wanted to remind you of the potential risks. As a leader, you should be aware of all the dangers you face, and face them together with those by your side.' 'How should I continue the assault from the front, then?' 'It's simple. Have some people lie in wait atop the cliffs, and throw down roadblocks from above when the enemy comes around to attack you from behind. That would both cut them off from their main force and protect your rear. 'Naturally, your retreat will be cut off too, but the fact that the enemy has split their troops simply makes them more vulnerable to a frontal assault by your main force. Victory is yours as long as you can defeat them before their troops can return to reinforce.' 'Sounds like a great idea! Let's go with that. I thought you were just a doctor, Harold. Where did you learn all this?' 'To tell the truth, I've led troops into battle before, but I found medicine to be far more interesting.' 'That so? Well, I love battles, and so do the other kids.' 'I would love war too, if all wars were as adorable. In any case, good luck, General Myrtle.' Why is Harold getting along so well with Myrtle and her group of wargaming children?
text.zh:
“将军，我刚才听您说，您打算从正面进攻对方的关口，所以想要说两句。”
“你是……那个军医？你觉得我的决策有问题？”
“不不，将军威名远播，我只是提出一些我的看法。您请看，这是战场的地形，一个正面的隘口，以及三条可以从侧面进出的小道。
“如果我是敌方，我知道以正面进攻而闻名的将军是自己的对手，必定会在加强隘口守备的同时，派人分别通过小道，绕到将军背后，形成前后夹击的态势。”
“唔，你说的确实有点道理。所以你的意思是，我应该分散队伍，分出人手从小道进攻？”
“不不不，只有三流的战术家才会认为，追求多变，让敌人无迹可寻是战术的极致。殊不知，唯有多智近妖者能做到欺骗所有人，实际上，一个人做事必然会留下属于他的痕迹。”
“听不懂。”
“很简单，就算我建议您分散队伍进攻，您愿意吗？”
“不愿意，太无聊了。”
“正是如此。我的提醒只是希望您能注意到可能存在的危机，身为一名领袖，您应当知道自己面临的所有危险，然后，与身边的人共同面对。”
“告诉我，哈洛德军医，有什么办法能让我继续正面突破？”
“很简单，您只需要分出一些人马埋伏在山崖上，在对方的队伍已经抵达您的背后想要进行偷袭时，从山崖上投下障碍物，切断他们与您大部队的联系，到那时，对方的夹击之势自然就化解了。
“虽然您的退路也会因此受阻，但是，因为对方分派出了人手进行伏击，他们的正面力量必定是不如您的大部队的，只要您能在对方的偷袭队伍赶回来以前消灭对方，那么胜利就是您的囊中之物。”
“听起来好像确实是这么一回事，那就听你的！哈洛德，你不是医生吗，这些你是从哪里学来的？”
“将军，不瞒您说，我以前也带过一些人打过一些仗，但是对我来说，考虑这些东西远不如当个医生有意思。”
“是吗？我觉得打仗很好玩啊，其他孩子也都很喜欢。”
“哈哈哈，如果这片大地上都是这样可爱的战争，我也会喜欢的。无论如何，祝您旗开得胜，桃金娘大将军。”

哈洛德为啥和桃金娘带起来的那群喜欢玩战争游戏的孩子混得那么好啊？！

text.en:
Oh, it's my turn?
What were we talking about again?
Ah, yes, each of us tells a story about ourselves. Spare me the look of anticipation, please. They say I've seen a lot, but it's nothing compared to what you've seen.
Wait, what's that vintage you just took out? Alright, very well, here's one I save for special occasions.
When I was young, I didn't have the slightest doubt about my duty. I believed I was fighting for Victoria, for the greater good, until I lost my leg.
There's really nothing remarkable about the story. I stepped on a mine, lost a leg, spent a few months in bed, then went back to the frontlines after getting a prosthetic limb. It's a rare soldier who isn't missing a piece here or there, but I rarely tell people what I was thinking at the time.
While I was lying in the doctor's tent like a mannikin, I saw for the first time my comrades being brought in, moaning in pain. Some of them recovered, others were taken away still moaning in pain, and yet others ended up with a white cloth draped over their face.
For the first time, I realized that when you stripped away the glamorous exterior of glory, all that's left is the pained cries of the soldiers, and hands dropping weakly off the sides of beds.
That was when I started to feel exhausted by war.
...We've come this far, Doctor. Let me say a little more.
I still remember the puzzled gazes upon me when I stepped into the world of high society for the first time. They were sharper than any sword and threatened to impale me, but I took it on the chin and kept walking.
To give your life for your country is an honor, but it should be by choice. No one was born to be sent to their death.
The reason I'm still working so hard at this age is to find a place for the poor bastards who've stuck it out with me all these years with so little to show for it, and to set my own mind at ease.
Now, don't give me that look, I'm thankful that Rhodes Island is willing to accept a bunch of old invalids like us, with all the limbs we don't have. Besides, your burden's hardly any lighter than mine. Who's pitying who here?
As someone who's been there, though, the only advice I can give you is this: There's no greater happiness than being able to eat, drink, walk, and sleep. To have a few true friends, and a couple stiff drinks.
A toast to your health, that we may see the sun rise again tomorrow.
text.zh:
嗯？轮到我说了吗？
等等，要说些什么来着？
噢，对了，每人讲一个自己的故事。哎，博士，别用那种期待的眼神看我，他们都说我见多识广，但和你波澜壮阔的经历相比，我实在是汗颜啊。
什么，你居然把这样的好酒拿出来了？唉，好吧，只能把这个压箱底的活计拿出来了！
年轻的时候，我曾对自己的使命坚信不疑，我相信我是在为了维多利亚而战，我是在为了一个崇高的目标而战，直到我失去了这条腿。
这个故事没有什么出奇的地方，我在战场上不慎被绊雷炸断了一条腿，在病床上躺了几个月后，换上假肢重回前线。对于一个士兵来说，身上不少点什么才是少见的事，但我很少给人讲那几个月中我想了什么。
当我像一个傀儡一样躺在医疗帐篷里时，我第一次看到我的战友一个个呻吟着被送了进来。他们有的康复了，有的又呻吟着被抬了出去，有的则被盖上了白布。
我第一次意识到，所谓的荣耀褪下那一层光鲜的外衣之后，剩下的竟然只是士兵们的哀嚎，和一双双无力垂下的手。
那是我人生中第一次对战争产生了一点厌倦。
……都说到这里了，就让我多说一点吧，博士。
直到今天，我依然记得，我第一次踏进社交场时，那一双双投向我的讶异视线。它们比任何刀剑都要锐利，简直要洞穿我的身体。但我还是硬着头皮，走了进去。
为国捐躯确实是一种荣耀，但这应该是一种选择，没有人生来就是为了被撵着去送死。
到了这个年纪我还在东奔西走，无非是想给这帮跟了我一辈子没怎么享过福的倒霉蛋们找一条退路，也好给我自己一个交代。
哈哈，别露出那副表情，罗德岛愿意接纳这群缺胳膊少腿的老病号，我已经十分感激了。况且，你肩上的东西，可一点不比我少，咱们谁同情谁可不好说啊，哈哈。
不过啊，博士，说来说去，说到最后，我作为过来人，能给你的建议只有一个：能吃能喝，能走能睡。有亲朋几个，有好酒两杯，其实就没有比这更幸福的事了。
来，干杯，敬我们还能看到明天的太阳。

text.en:
Come now, Doctor, it's not as if we only met yesterday. Do you truly believe that I'm a noble at heart? Just the thought of it is more chilling than a bottle of the stiff stuff straight out of the fridge.
These cans and bottles? Well, you know, you need the right perfumes and mouthwash for when you've drunk so much that you don't dare go home and face your wife's wrath. And you need the right cosmetics for when you're down with a hangover, but have a banquet to get to that you can't miss.
I learned this from the other nobles, of course. It's only when I became part of high society that I realized that being dressed in the finest livery doesn't make you any nobler than my foul-mouthed men.
Come, have a seat, and let me tell you what these are for. First, this bottle of perfume. Oh, I remember how it practically saved my life from my wife...
text.zh:
天哪，博士，我们已经认识有段时间了，难道你还相信我骨子里是一个贵族吗？这简直比刚从冰箱里取出来的酒还让人寒心。
你说这些瓶瓶罐罐？呃，是这样的，博士，当你因为喝多了而不敢回家面对夫人的怒火时，你也会需要一些合适的香水和漱口水。而当你宿醉醒来脸色苍白，脑子也不太清醒，却要去参加一个相当重要的宴会时，化妆就是必不可少的了。
当然，这些也是其他贵族传授给我的，真的步入社交场后我才发现，那些衣着光鲜的人私底下未必比我那些满口脏话的手下高贵。
好了，博士，坐吧，我来向你详细介绍一下这些东西各自有什么用途。首先是这瓶香水，啊，它可以说是在我夫人那里救过我的命……
